correctness.rationale: The assigned exact matrix is invertible. Reconstructing the subresultant condition in symmetric secant coordinates yields one genuine primitive degree-10 factor and only the stated cubic power of a linear leading-coefficient degeneration. Modulo \(19\) the degree-10 factor is irreducible, giving transitivity and a 10-cycle; modulo \(17\) it factors into irreducible degrees \(7\) and \(3\), giving a 7-cycle after cubing. A transitive degree-10 subgroup containing a 7-cycle is primitive; Jordan's theorem then gives \(A_{10}\), and the odd 10-cycle forces the full \(S_{10}\).
